experimental_method: Gas chromatographic determination of water in a vapour phase equilibrated with water in a rocking, windowed 316 stainless-steel cell at 160 F; vapour sample expanded through heated lines into a chromatograph (Carbowax 400 on Teflon column, helium carrier), calibrated by saturating methane/helium/CH4-H2S mixtures with water at atmospheric pressure at fixed temperatures.
uncertainties_stated: Per-point maximum-minimum deviation of individual samples is printed in the table (column); chromatograph response linear from 0 to about 43,000 ppm water.
quality_remarks: Pure-methane check measurements (to 1,495 psia at 160 F) agreed with Olds, Sage and Lacey (shown only in Fig. 4, not tabulated). Authors note the effect of H2S on water content is smaller than expected from theory. Water used as confining fluid for CH4-H2S runs, so H2S and CH4 dissolved in the water; vapour composition varied with pressure. Basis of the ppm unit and of 'per cent' H2S is not stated in the table or text; Fig. 4 caption says mole percent H2S and plots mole fraction of water. Only 6 data points, system is outside the plain gas list (CH4 + H2S).
not_extracted_tables: Fig. 4 (methane and CH4-H2S water content at 160 F, including the pure-methane verification points): a figure, no tabulated values; Fig. 1 literature comparison: figure.
